bounds: One notification group, three allocated row IDs, wall clock 0 through 2, one queued write, two non-silent inputs and representative silent, permanent, explicit-expiry and count-override inputs. Triage uses all nine supported categories, default or four explicit priorities, unspecified/permanent/explicit expiry, one admitted row, a three-value wall clock that can move in either direction, and read/unread state.
fairness: RequestFinishes assumes weak fairness of the serial writer's successful settlement. An admitted write can wait forever without fairness. AdmissionSettles assumes weak fairness of successful persistence in the triage case.
limitations: This case projects a row to its identity, title, silent priority, expiration, count and read mark. Exact projection uses the approval owner's unread, permanent, no-coalesced-count predicate.

The grouped case advances wall time monotonically. The triage case checks clock corrections in both directions without pruning durable history. A default silent lifetime is one model tick. The real SQLite scenario checks all 135 category, priority and expiry combinations with the actual 24-hour interval.
Write failure and ambiguous persistence are in NotificationDurability. Tenant ownership, cross-process writers, mixed group histories and arbitrary callbacks are outside this case.

assumptions: No fairness. A change in visibility leaves the retained row until a later write.
No fairness. Check the completed write transition and use the wall clock at that transition.
Assume weak fairness of settle after admission. This case assumes storage accepts the write.
No fairness. The serial writer can stutter forever after admission.
No fairness. A clock correction changes visibility without mutating the retained row.
Weak fairness of persist. This case assumes storage can accept the write. NotificationDurability covers persistence failures.
